lines.text: When you toss a plastic water bottle into the blue recycling bin, where does it actually go?
A collection truck transports it to a Materials Recovery Facility packed with robotic conveyor belts.
Optical infrared scanners shoot light beams through the plastics, identifying PET plastic in milliseconds.
High-pressure air jets shoot the bottle into designated bins, where it gets crushed into giant cubes.
The bales are shredded into microscopic plastic flakes, washed in hot caustic baths, and melted into pellets.
Those pellets get spun into polyester yarn for fleece jackets, carpets, or molded into brand new bottles.
Recycling a single bottle saves enough energy to power a laptop for three straight hours.
